static_traits.name: Lin Jiayi
static_traits.family_status: Lives with family in Florida, USA; family is fairly supportive, but she finds it hard to confide academic distress to her family
static_traits.social_status: Distancing from friends and classmates due to perceived inadequacy
static_traits.medical_history: Without major physical illness; without similar prior psychological problems or treatment history
static_traits.language_features: Initially slightly tense but willing to express, clear narration, good logic, self-reflective ability; self-labeling and negative automatic thoughts present; high cooperativeness, positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: My performance in science class makes me feel incompetent and low in self-worth; this feeling started this semester and appears almost daily, especially after receiving feedback on science homework.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of incompetence are affecting my self-esteem and learning motivation.
growth_experiences: At the start of the semester I had high self-expectations for science academics; as homework and test scores fell below expectations, these results gradually reinforced the belief 'I am not smart', with negative experiences appearing almost daily, accompanied by anxiety and disrupted sleep and diet rhythms.
The family as a whole is fairly supportive, but she finds it hard to express academic distress to family, which somewhat limits access to external emotional support.

special_situations.event: Receiving low-score feedback on science homework or quizzes
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If my grades are not good, it shows I am not smart
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Studies harder and seeks extra help from teachers, trying to prove self through effort
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am stupid / I am not smart enough

special_situations.event: When starting or doing science-related tasks (such as exam preparation, homework)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail again this time, it proves I can never learn science well
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids interacting with friends, studies hard alone, while worrying continuously
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely mess up/I will fail

special_situations.event: Recalling good performances in some quizzes or when understanding certain concepts
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Scattered good performances do not count; overall not good equals not smart
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores positive evidence, focuses only on negative grades and feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These decent performances are meaningless; I still cannot do it

special_situations.event: Facing the high standards I set for science yet not achieving them
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should get the ideal high score, otherwise it is failure and stupidity
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubly hard work, extending study time, to meet the 'should' standard
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should do better, or I am stupid

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be seen as capable, recognized and accepted
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being judged as stupid, dismissed, and humiliated
defense_goal: Through self-isolation, reduces threats from outside evaluation
Maintaining a sense of control over self-worth through excessive studying

object_relations.self_representation: Not smart enough, a learner prone to failure
object_relations.object_representation: Others with judgment and standards (teachers, classmates, family)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing science grades or asked to examine evidence of 'smart/capable'
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will think I am not smart enough, and I will be dismissed
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a self-blaming tone, lowering the voice, repeatedly using self-deprecating expressions (e.g. 'I am not smart enough'), downplaying others' positive feedback, rarely expressing dissatisfaction with external evaluations.

manifestations: Proactively distancing from friends and classmates due to perceived inadequacy
Finds it hard to open up to supportive family about academic distress, reducing access to external support
outcomes: Damaged self-esteem and reduced sense of self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent Self-denial in narration (e.g. 'I am not smart enough')
Initially tense, expressing carefully, worrying about 'saying wrong / not doing well'
Positive evidence is downplayed; keeps harshly blaming oneself

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Choosing to bear academic pressure alone and distancing from peers
Knowing there is family support but finding it hard to ask for help, turns pressure inward into self-blame and self-pressure

exception_events.target_problem: In science learning and test situations, the client usually falls into 'I am not smart enough' thoughts and feels anxious, with affected attention and decreased drive.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At moments of some quizzes and understanding certain science concepts, the client was not yet completely trapped by negative thoughts as before, but performed 'okay / understood well', gaining a degree of mastery.
exception_events.reason: Cues: had put in extra study effort and sought help from the teacher; when tasks are more focused or concepts are explained clearly, it is easier to gain a sense of mastery and positive feedback.

positive_force: The family as a whole is fairly supportive
Study motivation is still present, willing to work harder and proactively seek help
Able to identify and try restructuring negative thoughts (willing to do behavioral experiments)
Has successful experience in some quizzes and concept understanding, has ability evidence
negative_force: Self-labeling and all-or-nothing ability evaluation standards
Tends to ignore positive evidence and focus only on negative feedback
Catastrophic / predictive worry about future failure
Social avoidance leading to decreased support, further amplifying helplessness
Sleep and diet disturbed, lowering study efficiency and emotional tolerance

target_behavior.behavior: Academic-related anxiety and self-deprecation (e.g. 'I am not smart enough / I am stupid')
antecedent: Receiving low-score feedback on science homework or quizzes
When starting to prepare science homework, quizzes, or exams
target_behavior.core_reason: The labeling belief that equates academic grades with intelligence and self-worth, and the black-and-white standard for evaluating ability
target_behavior.function: Escapes the threat of being evaluated, gains temporary control over self-worth
target_behavior.consequence: Learning motivation and focus decline, negative emotions intensify, forming a vicious cycle of 'low performance - negative beliefs'

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance (distancing from friends and classmates)
antecedent: Talking about or thinking of unsatisfactory science grades on campus
Anticipating peers or others will evaluate my academic ability
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being seen as 'not smart', avoiding social evaluation to reduce shame and anxiety
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome social evaluation and possible exposure of failure
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced social support, increased loneliness, further aggravating helplessness and low self-esteem

antecedent: Persistent tension and rumination when studying or reviewing science tasks
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic predictions and persistent worry about failure and inadequacy, finding it hard to emotionally relax
target_behavior.function: Physically reflects stress and vigilance, trying to prepare for 'avoiding failure'
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased mental and cognitive efficiency, further affecting learning performance and reinforcing negative beliefs
